items.statement: Replacing four of eight faculty sessions with calibrated near-peer sessions keeps the first-attempt pass rate on examination-skills stations within 5 percentage points of faculty-only teaching while lowering the teaching cost per student.
items.rationale: The retrieved randomised comparison and costing point this way, but neither was designed as an economic evaluation with a fair local comparison.
items.risks: One year of students cannot give a precise effect; calibration may not be delivered as planned.

items.statement: Valuing tutor time at the research assistant rate will not reverse the cost advantage of the near-peer option.
items.rationale: The costing record reports 19 against 46 units with tutor time valued; novelty is not rated because it depends on local pay rates not yet supplied.

items.statement: Near-peer teaching will release at least 60 faculty sessional hours per year.
items.rationale: Four sessions for 18 groups of 10 students would otherwise need faculty time.
items.risks: Faculty supervision of tutors takes back part of the time released.

summary: Three hypotheses; one novelty judgement is left unrated (null) because the local pay rate is not known.
